requirement: A university manages students enrolling in courses. Each student has a Student ID, Name, and Major. Each course has a Course Code, Title, and Credits. A student can enroll in many courses and a course can have many students; for each enrollment the system records the Semester and the Grade.

A school organizes departments and the teachers who work in them. Each department has a Department ID, Name, and Office Location. Each teacher has a Teacher ID, Name, and Title, and belongs to exactly one department. A department can have many teachers.

A university schedules course sections taught by teachers. Each course has a Course Code and Title. Each teacher has a Teacher ID and Name. A section has a Section ID, Semester, Room, and Schedule; each section belongs to one course and is taught by one teacher.

A course management system records assignments and the grades students receive. Each assignment has an Assignment ID, Title, and Max Score. Each student has a Student ID and Name. A student submits many assignments and an assignment is submitted by many students; for each submission the system records the Submission Date and Score.

A university assigns each student an academic advisor. Each student has a Student ID, Name, and Enrollment Year. Each advisor has an Advisor ID, Name, and Office. Each student is advised by exactly one advisor, and an advisor can advise many students.

A library lends books to students. Each book has an ISBN, Title, and Author. Each student has a Student ID and Name. A loan has a Loan ID, Borrow Date, and Due Date; each loan is for one book borrowed by one student. A student can have many loans and a book can be loaned many times.

An online learning platform organizes courses into modules and lessons. Each course has a Course ID and Title. Each module has a Module ID, Title, and Order Number, and belongs to one course. Each lesson has a Lesson ID, Title, and Duration, and belongs to one module.

A university defines prerequisite relationships between courses. Each course has a Course Code, Title, and Credits. A course can require many other courses as prerequisites, and a course can be a prerequisite for many courses.

A school records exams and the rooms where they are held. Each exam has an Exam ID, Subject, and Exam Date. Each room has a Room Number, Building, and Capacity. An exam is held in exactly one room, and a room can host many exams.

A university tracks degree programs and the students pursuing them. Each program has a Program ID, Name, and Degree Level. Each student has a Student ID, Name, and Admission Date, and is enrolled in exactly one program. A program can have many students.

A school manages student clubs and their members. Each club has a Club ID, Name, and Founded Year. Each student has a Student ID and Name. A student can join many clubs and a club can have many members; for each membership the system records the Join Date and Role.

A university records class attendance. Each section has a Section ID and Subject. Each student has a Student ID and Name. An attendance record has a Class Date and Status (present or absent), captured for one student in one section. A student attends many sessions of a section.
